I wrote the 60-minute lesson on O3, but I think it may be short of the target length, and I couldn't count the words. I wrote about 6,000 words and added four extra practice tasks to push it up. The bench accepts 5,400 to 13,500 words for a 60-minute lesson, and I think this lands just inside it. Nothing was run or opened in a browser, so the page's checks and figures are untested.

**Lesson:** `lessons/0001-context-and-memory-in-an-agent.html`

It has six concept sections. Each opens with a traced example, then the name, a "Why this works" box and a check question:
1. **The context window**: what the model sees in one call.
2. **What is kept between steps**: your program resends the history on every call. A three-call request totals 7,040 input tokens.
3. **Context rot**: why a bigger window is not better.
4. **Compaction**: summarizing old history to make room.
5. **Notes**: saving short, lasting facts so they carry into the next session. This uses Python and a JSON file, with the example of a student's training status.
6. **Retrieval**: pulling manual chunks in on demand with a small search tool.

It also has a warm-up from your agent-loop record, a worked example (sorting each fact in a request into context, notes or retrieval) and a faded practice task. It ends with a summary and the sources.

The token counts and the failure scenario in the lesson are made-up illustrations, and the lesson labels them that way. The sources are Anthropic's [context engineering post](https://anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents) and the [Claude context window docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows). The [contextual retrieval post](https://anthropic.com/research/contextual-retrieval) is only linked as further reading, from a search result I did not open.

I also added `cheatsheets/context-and-memory.html`, created `RESOURCES.md`, and added a line to `NOTES.md`. Embedding-based search and better retrieval methods are left for a later lesson.

Ask me for a quiz when you're ready, or ask me anything about the lesson.

One question: should I look for a community where you can try agent designs? `RESOURCES.md` has none yet.
